findings.result: Expo Modules Core 3.0.30 AnyFrontendConvert::convert at FrontendConverter.cpp:559–617 recurses with itself for array/object values. After bool/number/string checks it calls asObject. Nested null/undefined do not use the separate NullableFrontendConverter at632–649. The native method accepts Map<String,Any?> at BoomerangModule.kt:34; that outer nullable map value does not recursively make nested Any nullable.

memoryMovieExport.ts:116 constructs each scene with backgroundUri undefined for non-video scenes and audio pageAudio, which can be undefined. The top request at 129 includes optional soundtrack. This matches the nested-absent-value boundary being repaired.

composeMemoryMovie still validates the original request before projection and dispatch. Explicit projection covers every current request, scene, StoryVideoRecipe, motion, transition, artwork-window, audio and soundtrack-gain field. No type-defined field is discarded. Invalid artwork animation is rejected before a projection could remove it.

Only null/undefined optional scene.backgroundUri, scene.audio and request.soundtrack are omitted. Present typed fields are copied directly, preserving 0 volume/start/offset/fade, false loop, negative offsets/matrix coefficients and original array order.

A new request object, scenes array/objects, recipe/matrix, layers, transition, motion, audio, soundtrack and gain windows are allocated. No original request mutation occurs. Cancellation identity and result validation use the submitted snapshot, so caller edits while native work is pending cannot redirect cancel or change the expected output/timeline.

Capability gate, original request validator, pre-aborted rejection, single abort listener/removal, native cancellation and late-success rejection remain. Export access/rights checks before and after compose and before saving are unchanged upstream; native validation and unsupported animation restrictions remain intact.
